parsedVerdict.reasoning: AppointmentsController behaves like a thin presentation controller. It defines the input shapes (BookingForm, NoteForm) and turns transport values into the types the service expects, such as `new Date(form.startsAt)`. It then hands the actual work to the business services SchedulingService and VisitNotesService, and formats the results with the presenter. It contains no business rules: it does no validation of scheduling conflicts, cancellation policy or note rules. It also has no persistence or framework logic. The `count` returned by addNote is just the length of the service result, packaged for the response. Passing `new Date()` as the cancellation time only supplies the request context to the service. Every responsibility in the file fits the presentation layer.
